correctness.rationale: The finite cube has the cited homotopy type. Coordinatewise clamping is 1-Lipschitz and induces a simplicial retraction; on all other selected cubes it is constant. The retractions jointly define a left inverse to the inclusion of the direct sum because each finite chain is collapsed by all sufficiently distant retractions. The countable simplicial chain groups give the matching upper bound on rank in degrees \(4\) and \(7\).

evidence: The lattice paper notes that inclusion of one binary cube induces homology injection at every scale.
The hypercube theorem gives positive ranks \(b_4(n)\) and \(b_7(n)\) for each \(n\ge5\).
Coordinatewise clamping to C_k is 1-Lipschitz, fixes C_k, and is constant on every other selected cube C_j.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The single-cube injection gives only one finite-rank summand. The retractions for infinitely many translated cubes are jointly split because each finite chain is sent to a point by all sufficiently distant retractions; this yields a direct sum of countably many cube homology groups.

value.motivation: Question 5.2 in arXiv:2511.04238v1 asks for a countable wedge of \(S^4\) and \(S^7\); the result proves that each of those degrees has the required infinite rank.
value.rationale: The claim resolves a precise, necessary homological part of an explicit open question about the scale-three integer-lattice Rips complex. It upgrades the known single-cube injection to a split direct sum of infinitely many independent cube contributions and establishes exact countably infinite ranks in \(\widetilde H_4\) and \(\widetilde H_7\). It does not overstate this as a full homotopy classification.
